{{Short description|American researcher}}
'''Steven M. Bachrach''' is an [[organic chemist]] who took up the position of Dean of Science at [[Monmouth University]] in 2016.  Bachrach had previously been the Dr D. R. Semmes Distinguished Professor of Chemistry at [[Trinity University (Texas)|Trinity University]] in San Antonio, Texas.<ref name = Bio />  Bachrach is the author of the textbook ''Computational Organic Chemistry''.<ref name = COCtext />

== Education ==
Bachrach earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree from the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] and a [[PhD]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name = Bio />

== Career ==
Bachrach is an [[organic chemist]] specializing in [[computational organic chemistry]] and began his career at [[Northern Illinois University]], where he earned a [[Professorship]].  He spent 17 years at [[Trinity University (Texas)|Trinity University]], holding positions including the Dr. D. R. Semmes Distinguished Professor of Chemistry, Chair of the Department of Chemistry, and Assistant Vice-President for Special Projects.  He then took up the position of Dean of Science in 2016 at [[Monmouth University]].<ref name = Bio>{{cite web|url = https://www.monmouth.edu/directory/profiles/steven-m-bachrach/|title = Steven M. Bachrach, PhD|date = |accessdate = June 1, 2021|publisher = [[Monmouth University]]}}</ref> Bachrach departed from Monmouth University in 2022 and currently holds the position of Dean, Artis College of Science and Technology at [[Radford University]].<ref name = CurrentPosition>{{cite web|url = https://www.radford.edu/president/university-leadership.html/|title = Steven M. Bachrach, PhD|date = |accessdate = October 17, 2024|publisher = [[Radford University]]}}</ref>

== Computational organic chemistry ==
[[File:Bachrach image of hexamethylbenzene dication.png|right|thumb|250px|Bachrach's illustration of {{chem|C|6|(CH|3|)|6|2+}}, the dication of [[hexamethylbenzene]]<ref name = BachrachHMB />]]
Bachrach has written a textbook about computational organic chemistry, the second edition of which was published by [[John Wiley and Sons]] in 2014.<ref name = COCtext>{{cite book|year = 2014|first = Steven|last = Bachrach|authorlink = Steven Bachrach|title = Computational Organic Chemistry|edition = 2nd|isbn = 9781118291924|publisher = [[John Wiley & Sons]]}}</ref>  Bachrach maintains a [[blog]] to provide supplementary materials for the textbook.<ref>{{cite web|title = About "Computational Organic Chemistry" blog|last = Bachrach|first = Steven M.|authorlink = Steven Bachrach|url = http://comporgchem.com/blog/?page_id=2|accessdate = January 18, 2017|date = April 5, 2009|website = comporgchem.com}}</ref>  For example, following the publication of the structure of the [[dication]] of [[hexamethylbenzene]], {{chem|C|6|(CH|3|)|6|2+}},  in ''[[Angewandte Chemie International Edition]]'',<ref>{{cite journal|title = Crystal Structure Determination of the Pentagonal-Pyramidal Hexamethylbenzene Dication C<sub>6</sub>(CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>6</sub><sup>2+</sup>|first1 = Moritz|last1 = Malischewski|first2 = Konrad|last2 = Seppelt|authorlink2 = Konrad Seppelt|journal = [[Angew. Chem. Int. Ed.]]|volume = 56|issue = 1|pages = 368–370|year = 2017|doi = 10.1002/anie.201608795|pmid = 27885766}}</ref> Bachrach discussed its [[pyramidal carbocation|pyramidal geometry]] and six-coordinate carbon [[moiety (chemistry)|moiety]] in a blog post, demonstrating it is not [[Hypervalent molecule|hypervalent]] and explaining its three-dimensional [[aromaticity]].<ref name = BachrachHMB>{{cite web|title = A six-coordinate carbon atom|last = Bachrach|first = Steven M.|authorlink = Steven Bachrach|url = http://comporgchem.com/blog/?page_id=3929|accessdate = January 18, 2017|date = January 17, 2017|website = comporgchem.com}}</ref>
